analysis.title: Weekly Automotive Pit Stop: Key themes from week 1 of auto earnings
key_insights: BofA sees cost inflation emerging as a key 2027 risk for OEMs and suppliers. GM flagged a $1.0-1.5bn commodity headwind on its 3Q call, incremental to the ~$500mm-$1bn already in its original plan.
Steel is the largest exposure, with HRC up +4.1% since end of September and near four-year highs. Copper is hovering near record levels.

Raw material inputs for an average vehicle reached $4,845 at end of September, up +1% MoM and +32% YoY, and BofA thinks the current figure is likely higher. 1Q27 is seen as the largest YoY commodity headwind quarter, with pricing, supplier negotiations and efficiencies as potential offsets.

BofA expects Ford to highlight a similar cost impact, with 2027 commentary likely tempered, and expects suppliers to flag rising cost inflation. DCH previously pointed to direct inflation and supply chain cost pressure.

A prolonged diesel spike adds cost and demand pressure across autos. Diesel was $6.28/gal as of 10/19, up 73.4% YoY and up ~65% since the Iran conflict began. GM said fuel hits logistics with a two to four week lag, a sizable part of its $400mm of incremental 2026 inflation.
Diesel spikes have historically coincided with softer HD truck sales. BofA expects fuel to remain a key theme in next week's earnings.

LAD's 3Q results partly confirmed BofA's concern that affordability is weighing on dealer parts and service. P&S gross grew +2%, customer count fell slightly, customer pay was flat, and growth came from higher average RO value rather than RO count.
LAD pointed to a shrinking vehicles in operation base, with the average vehicle in its service lane ~4 years old, matching the depressed 2022 SAAR after the chip crisis.

New Jersey's franchise law change, effective April 2026, requires OEMs to pay dealers warranty labor closer to retail rates. BofA thinks this could help LAD's warranty comps through 1Q27, and more states considering similar laws could make it a broader dealer P&S tailwind.
September US SAAR was 16.0mm, down from 16.8mm in August, above BofA's mid-month estimate of 15.9mm but below Bloomberg consensus of 16.4mm. YTD SAAR is 16.1mm vs 16.4mm in FY25.

BofA sees rising affordability concerns given the outlook for interest rate increases and high oil prices. Demand YTD has stayed resilient as wealthier consumers drive a larger share of new vehicle sales, alongside pent-up demand from an aging fleet.
By OEM in September, Honda sales rose +11.3% YoY and Hyundai +5.4%, while GM fell -4.1%, Ford -2.1%, Stellantis -6.1% and Tesla -29.6%. Toyota rose +4.0%.
Detroit Three share of US light vehicles was 37.1% in September vs 38.7% a year earlier, while Japanese OEMs gained to 37.2% from 34.5%.
US inventory at end of September rose 97k units MoM to 2.60mm, or 49 days' supply vs a 5-year average of 46. Ford is at 71DS and Stellantis at 84DS, vs GM at 65DS.
Detroit 3 inventory rose 71k MoM, led by GM (+37k) and Ford (+28k). Stellantis car inventory is at 198 days' supply.
Industry ATP was $50,562 in September, up +0.7% YoY and +0.9% MoM per KBB. Incentives were down -8.4% YoY but up +2.9% MoM, at 6.6% of ATP vs ~10% in 2019.
Hybrids remain the bright spot with demand up +38% YoY, while EV demand is down -44% YoY. Alternative powertrains are 24% of sales and ICE is 76%.
The Manheim used vehicle index was down -0.5% YoY and -1.1% MoM in September.
Mobility Global's 2026 global light vehicle production forecast rose +48bps since July, with China (-181bps) and North America (-49bps) cut and other regions raised.
EU/EFTA/UK BEV registrations rose +59.9% YoY in September to a 30.5% share. Chinese brands rose +75.3% YoY, lifting share to 16.0% from 10.0%.
China passenger car retail sales fell -27.8% YoY and BEV sales fell -7.4% YoY in September. Tesla China wholesale volume rose +5% YoY to 95k and Tesla Korea sales were 12.3k, up 36% YoY.

BofA's analysis suggests a 10%+ sequential gas price increase correlates with a 90bps reduction in the mix of larger vehicle purchases over the following six months. US retail gas is $4.42, up +44% since the Iran conflict, though gas is 2.1% of disposable income vs a ~2.8% historical average.
Consumer confidence (preliminary October) fell to 46.3, -14% YoY, while auto SAAR has held up, diverging from the long-term correlation.

market_movers.rationale: PO based on ~4.75x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates. BofA cites improving Model e losses, Ford Pro stability and a favorable US regulatory backdrop. Stock at $11.94.
PO based on ~10.2x P/E on 2027 estimates vs ~8.0x dealer through-cycle average, supported by earnings track record and M&A execution. Stock at $291.07.

sector_views.rationale: Cost inflation (commodities, diesel) is a building 2027 risk and affordability is weighing on dealer P&S, but SAAR has held up on wealthier consumers and an aging fleet.

earnings_insights: GM 3Q call: flagged a $1.0-1.5bn 2027 commodity headwind, incremental to ~$500mm-$1bn already in its original plan, and ~$400mm of incremental 2026 inflation partly from fuel logistics.
LAD 3Q (reported): P&S gross +2%, customer count down slightly, customer pay flat, growth from higher average RO value.
BofA expects Ford and suppliers to flag cost inflation in upcoming earnings next week, with Ford's 2027 commentary likely tempered (BofA expectation, not a reported figure).

Up 73.4% YoY and ~65% since the Iran conflict began, a cost and demand headwind for autos.
Down -1.1% WoW, up +44% since the Iran conflict.
Down -14% YoY, at record lows, yet auto SAAR has held up.

macro_indicators.indicator: Average raw material cost per vehicle
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up +1% MoM and +32% YoY per BofA estimates, signaling cost pressure for OEMs.

risk_factors: Rising commodity costs, especially steel (HRC near four-year highs) and copper (near record levels), into 2027.
Prolonged diesel spike raising logistics costs and softening HD truck demand.
Affordability pressure on consumers from interest rate increase expectations and high oil prices.
Shrinking vehicles in operation base weighing on dealer parts and service.
Ford downside risks: auto sales downturn, sharp input cost rise, supply base disruption, gas price spikes, pricing deterioration, share losses.
LAD downside risks: swift US sales downturn, slower operating leverage, domestic brand share loss, higher rates, franchise and consumer finance law changes.
charts_described: Exhibit 29: a 10%+ sequential increase in monthly gas prices correlates with a 90bps reduction in mix of larger vehicle purchases in the following 6 months vs the prior 6 months.
Exhibit 26: gasoline and other energy goods are 2.1% of disposable personal income as of August 2026, below the ~2.8% historical average.
Exhibit 20: auto SAAR has held up despite record low consumer confidence, diverging from the long-term correlation.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: diesel is up ~65% and gasoline up +44% since it began.
Vessel crossings through the Strait of Hormuz remain at depressed levels.

tension_points.bull_case: YTD demand has stayed resilient as wealthier consumers drive a larger share of new vehicle sales, with pent-up demand from an aging fleet. SAAR has held up despite record-low consumer confidence.
tension_points.bear_case: Affordability concerns are rising given the outlook for interest rate increases and high oil prices. Historically, large gas price increases correlate with lower SAAR and a smaller mix of large vehicles.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained further rise in gas prices, which BofA's analysis ties to a ~90bps drop in larger-vehicle mix over six months.
